text.p: Republican presidential challenger Bob Dole on Wednesday confidently predicted a come-from-behind victory over front-running President Bill Clinton in the Nov. 5 election "because we have the ideas."
And his running mate, Jack Kemp, went a step further in a morning television interview, saying overcoming a double-digit lead by Clinton would be "a piece of cake."

Dole was in a fighting mood before about 2,000 students jammed into an auditorium at St. Louis University on what was supposed to be the date of the first debate between Dole and Clinton at nearby Washington University. But they changed the date and place to Oct. 6 in Hartford, Connecticut.

The paths of Dole and Reform Party candidate Ross Perot, who blames Dole and a bipartisan debate commission for shutting him out of the debates, were to cross in this city. Perot planned to come to St. Louis University on Wednesday and continue his campaign to be included in the debates.

A few pro-Perot hecklers were in the audience but Dole told cheering fans "don't be distracted by the noises here, it's all going to be over and we're going to win, we're going to win because we have the ideas, because we have the agenda."
Dole pushed his economic package, centred on a 15 percent across-the-board income tax rate cut, a capital gains tax cut and a $500 per child tax credit.

Dole appeared in front of a 20-foot (6-meter) backdrop: "Dole-Kemp, The Dole agenda, keeping more of what you earn." He took off on that theme, contrasting his tax cut plans with that of his "liberal" opponent, Clinton, who he said wants to raise taxes.
Dole said his economic plan "is based on one simple belief -- it's your money, it's your money, it's your money."
Everyone will get the tax cut if Dole is elected, "even former President Clinton is going to get this tax cut back in Arkansas," the Republican candidate said.
Kemp said on ABC's "Good Morning America" that closing Clinton's double-digit lead in polls was "a piece of cake."
"I acknowledge the fight," Kemp said, but the numbers do not tell all. "They are very soft for the president," he said. "We are very confident ... that Bob Dole is going to win."
